b2-21-01.title: Communicative Challenge: A Rumour at the Office
b2-21-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you have heard about the director. You heard a rumour that the director is resigning tomorrow.
b2-21-01.prompt: Tell Carlos the rumour you heard.
cues: Say that it is a rumour
Say what the director is doing
b2-21-01.target: Dicen que el director renuncia mañana.
b2-21-01.english: They say the director is resigning tomorrow.
b2-21-01.canDo: I can use a plural verb with no subject for rumours and for unknown doers.

b2-21-02.title: Communicative Challenge: When You Are Tired
b2-21-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what happens when you are tired. You answer with a general remark: when you are tired, you work worse.
b2-21-02.prompt: Make a general remark to Carlos about working when you are tired.
cues: Say what happens to your work
b2-21-02.target: Cuando uno está cansado, trabaja peor.
b2-21-02.english: When you are tired, you work worse.
b2-21-02.canDo: I can choose between se, a plural verb and uno to say who is part of the statement.

b2-21-03.title: Communicative Challenge: What Worries People
b2-21-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what worries people in the city. You say that the rise in prices worries many people.
b2-21-03.prompt: Tell Meg what worries many people.
b2-21-03.target: La subida de los precios preocupa a muchas personas.
b2-21-03.english: The rise in prices worries many people.
b2-21-03.canDo: I can turn a verb clause into a noun phrase, as in la subida de los precios.

b2-21-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Planning a Party
b2-21-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what is needed for the party. You say that everyone needs to bring something to eat.
b2-21-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what is needed for the party.
b2-21-04.target: Hace falta que cada uno traiga algo de comer.
b2-21-04.english: Everyone needs to bring something to eat.
b2-21-04.canDo: I can use hace falta que, basta con que and urge que with the subjunctive.

b2-21-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Is the Plan Working?
b2-21-05.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks whether the plan is working. You are not completely sure, so you soften your answer and suggest checking the schedule.
b2-21-05.prompt: Answer Meg carefully and suggest checking the schedule.
b2-21-05.target: Parece que el plan funciona, pero tal vez convendría revisar el horario.
b2-21-05.english: It seems the plan is working, but perhaps it would be a good idea to check the schedule.
b2-21-05.canDo: I can soften a claim with parece que, según parece or podría decirse que.

b2-21-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Text About Céspedes
b2-21-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you read about Augusto Céspedes. You read that his book of stories was published in 1936.
b2-21-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos what you read about Céspedes and his book.
cues: Say what kind of book it is
b2-21-consolidation.target: Leí que el libro de cuentos de Céspedes se publicó en 1936.
b2-21-consolidation.english: I read that Céspedes's book of stories was published in 1936.
b2-21-consolidation.canDo: I can use a plural verb, se or uno to speak about unnamed people.
